items.summary: Jong Oranje heeft zich via de play-offs alsnog geplaatst voor het EK van aankomende zomer in Albanië en Servië. De ploeg van Michael Reiziger was in een tweeluik te sterk voor Jong Denemarken. In dit artikel lees je alles over de loting voor het EK Onder-21.

items.title: Selectie Besiktas komt in noodweer terecht: 'Een van de spannendste vluchten ooit'
items.summary: De voorbereiding van Besiktas op het Europa League-duel met Hapoel Be'er Sheva is flink verstoord geraakt. De Turkse selectie kwam tijdens de vlucht naar het Georgische Batumi midden in een onweersbui terecht en moest uitwijken. Vervolgens vervolgde Besiktas de reis van Rize naar Georgië over het asfalt.

items.title: Sneijder casht flink met verkoop shirts Ramos en Ronaldo

items.title: Rondje Europa Extra: 'Serie van vijf uitduels mag geen excuus zijn voor FC Twente'

items.title: Manchester United, Liverpool and Spurs using same law firm to set up legal claim against City
items.summary: Rivals engage law firm Wiggin as they seek damages Claim could be worth hundreds of millions of pounds Manchester United, Liverpool and Tottenham are using the same law firm to prepare a legal claim against Manchester City for breaking the Premier League’s financial rules that could be worth hundreds of millions of pounds. The clubs have engaged the services of the London-based media, entertainment and technology specialists Wiggin. Arsenal are using their retained lawyers, HFS Kramer, to prepare their own claim. Continue reading...

items.title: ‘We are on the edge’: how Swedish league declined from summit of women’s game
items.summary: The Damallsvenskan once mastered Europe and attracted the best players, but many are now worried for its future On 12 October 2003, Sweden stood still. The women’s football team were playing Germany in the World Cup final. TV4 set a new viewing record as almost half the nation watched the game go into extra time, where Nia Künzer scored the golden goal winner after 98 minutes. It was a bitter pill to swallow but there was still the belief that the tournament would mark the start of women’s football’s commercial breakthrough in Sweden. After all, how could sponsors and broadcasters ignore such undeniable interest? Continue reading...

items.title: Neville, Carragher and the inescapable podcasting feedback loop of doom | Jonathan Liew
items.summary: Even the best managers can struggle to escape ex-players’ need to manufacture a crisis for content. Enter Michael Carrick … A podcast studio in Manchester. A production runner pours water into jugs. Gary Neville enters the room with Michael Carrick. Neville: Just so you know, we’re already filming. This is the intro bit, where we show everyone coming on to set and doing some light banter. It humanises us. The viewer sees it and thinks we’re just mates chatting about football, rather than scions of a global podcast empire commercially obliged to produce an endless scroll of provocative content for money. I always say: why can’t you be both? Continue reading...

items.title: ‘Not Bayern-like’: Joshua Kimmich fumes at club’s treatment of Jamal Musiala
items.summary: Bundesliga champions lost 2-1 to Lille on Wednesday Kimmich defends Musiala’s neurological condition The Bayern Munich midfielder Joshua Kimmich has launched a stinging attack on the club’s “not Bayern-like” treatment of his teammate Jamal Musiala, who has a condition which causes seizures. Senior Bayern figures have publicly questioned Musiala’s performances and contract after repeated seizures caused by a neurological condition, including two on the field in pre-season games, drawing protests from the players’ union Fifpro. Now Kimmich, the club’s vice-captain, has spoken out and warned Bayern risked undermining their family image. Continue reading...

items.title: Titulaire avec les Diables Rouges U17, Maël Oppenbrouwer (Charleroi) suscite l'intérêt en Belgique
